sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 is filed seeking compensation of .1,00,00,000/- for the death of Mrunal Suneelkumar totad S/o Suneelkumar Sangappa totad in a road traffic accident.

2. It is specific case of the petition that on 28- 10-2023 at about 10:30 A.M., the deceased Mrunal Suneelkumar Totad was riding a motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22-HF-5538, near HP Petrol Bunk, BM old NH-275 road, Shivapura, Maddur Town, Mandya District.

At that time, the driver of the Tata vehicle bearing Registration No.HR-37-D-3194 (herein after called as offending vehicle) came from same direction in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly swerved from right lane to left lane and stopped the vehicle in the middle of the road.
As a result, the offending vehicle dashed the deceased's two-wheeler.
Due to the forceful impact, the deceased fell onto the road and sustained grievous injuries.
3. He was immediately shifted to Maddur Government Hospital, for first aid, thereafter referred to a hospital in Bengaluru hospital.

However, he succumbed to his injuries on the way to the hospital,
where a post-mortem was conducted.

Subsequently, his body was handed over to the petitioners,
and his last rites were performed.
4. The petitioners state that Petitioner No. 1 is the mother, and Petitioner No. 2 is the father of the deceased.
The deceased was hale and healthy, was working as a Engineer in Radisys India Ltd., and was earning Rs.25,000 per month.
The petitioners were financially and emotionally dependent on him.
Owing to his untimely demise, they have suffered immense mental shock and agony,loss of love and affection, and loss of the sole breadwinner of the family.
5. The petitioners further assert that they incurred an expenditure of Rs. 4,00,000/- towards transportation of the dead body, Funeral expenses, and obsequies ceremonies.
It is their contention that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly, the petitioners have prayed that this Court may be pleased to award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest, to be paid jointly and severally by Respondents No.
1 and No. 2, being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle.
6. In response to the petition, Respondent No. 2 appeared through counsel and filed the written statements.
Respondent No. 1 failed to appear and he placed exparte.

7. Respondent No. 2 in its written statement, denied the involvement of offending vehicle and issuance of the insurance policy from its branch, but liability is strictly subject to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and also confirmation of policy from the branch office.
The Respondent no 2 alleged that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased.
It has contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of the motorcycle were not arrayed as respondents.

2 8. The insurer has further submitted that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not in possession of a valid driving licence and it has no valid permit and FC, thereby violating policy conditions.
The Respondent no 2 has denied the age, income, and occupation of the deceased as claimed in the petition.
The dependency of the petitioners on the deceased was also put to strict proof.
The amount of compensation claimed was termed excessive, arbitrary.

Accordingly,
Respondent No. 2 has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

9. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that the death of Mrunal Suneelkumar Totad S/o.
Suneelkumar Sangappa Totad, was only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tata vehicle bearing No.HR-37- D-3194 on 28-10-2023, about 10.30 a.m. Bengaluru-Mysuru old NH 275 Road, near HP Petrol Bunk, Shivapura Maddur Town, Mandya District?
2. What compensation petitioners are entitled?
3. What order ?
10.
In support of their claim, 1st Petitioner was examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.15.
Eyewitness /pillion rider of motorcycle is examined as PW-2 and got marked Ex.P.16 and employer is examined as PW-3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.17 to 20.
11. On the other hand, the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.
12. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

13. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 14. ISSUE NO.1:- PW-1 has stated that on 28- 10-2023 at about 10:30 A.M., the deceased Mrunal Suneelkumar Totad was riding a motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22-HF-5538, near HP Petrol Bunk, BM old NH-275 road, Shivapura, Maddur Town, Mandya District.

At that time, the driver of the offending vehicle came from same direction in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly swerved from right lane to left lane and stopped the vehicle in the middle of the road.
As a result, the offending vehicle dashed the deceased's two-wheeler.
Due to the forceful impact, the deceased fell onto the road and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries.

sentences.text:
PW1 has relied upon the police documents marked at Exhibits P1 to P9, which include the FIR,
FIS, Crime Details Form, Spot Mahazar, Seizure Mahazar, Spot Sketch, IMV Report, Inquest Report,
Post-Mortem Report and the Charge Sheet.
The petitioner has placed strong reliance on these police records, which collectively indicate that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

16. On the contrary, Respondent No. 2 has taken a specific contention that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased rider and not due to any fault on the part of the driver of the offending TATA vehicle.
Respondent No. 2 asserts that the deceased himself was negligent and was solely responsible for the accident.
17. To substantiate the manner of the accident, the petitioners examined the eyewitness, who was the pillion rider on the motorcycle, as PW-2.
She has categorically stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the TATA vehicle bearing registration No. HR-37-D-3194.
She has supported the version reflected in the police records and confirmed that the offending TATA vehicle was being driven in a rash and negligent manner.
18. During the course of cross-examination of PW-1, Learned Counsel for Respondent No. 2 put forth a suggestion that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
However, PW-1 denied the same.
Similarly, a suggestion was made to PW-2 that she was not an eyewitness and was not travelling as a pillion rider, which she also denied.
She further denied that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.

19. The petitioner has submitted that, after a thorough investigation, the police filed a charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle, clearly indicating that the accident was caused by the negligence of the said driver.
Due to the said accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and ultimately succumbed to them.

20. Having considered the rival contentions and upon re-appreciation of the material available on record, it is seen that except for the suggestions made in cross-examination and the bare contentions in the objections, the Respondent Insurance Company has not produced any evidence to disprove the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

There is no material on record to discredit the evidence of the petitioners or to substantiate the contention of Respondent No. 2.
21.
The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 is consistent, corroborative, and duly supported by the documents produced by the petitioners.
Nothing has been elicited in cross-examination to disprove their version.

It is a well-settled principle that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation, and the Court should not insist on strict proof of rashness and negligence as required in criminal trials.

The investigation clearly concluded that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, and there is no evidence before the Court to show that the deceased was negligent or solely responsible.
22. Therefore, the contention raised by the Respondent Insurance Company holds no water.

The Tribunal concludes that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending Arati Suneelkumar Totad vs Suresh on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134448561/
4 TATA vehicle, resulting in the injuries and subsequent death of the deceased. Hence I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
23.
ISSUE No.2:- Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father of deceased.
In order to substantiate their relationship, PW-1 has produced the inquest report, Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners and deceased, they are marked at Ex.P.12 to 14.
The recital of the said record shows that deceased Mrunal Suneelkumar Totad was the son of Petitioners.
Petitioner no 1 and 2 - parents of the deceased have stated that deceased was hale and healthy, and working as a Software Engineer in Radysis India Ltd., and earning .28,000/-Per month.
The Petitioner No.1 and 2 are financially and emotionally dependent on the deceased.

24. On perusal of records, it is found that Petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased at Ex.P.14, which shows the date of birth as 11-05- 2000 and as such, age of the deceased is considered as 23 years at the time of accident and appropriate multiplier applicable is 18.
25.
It is stated that the petitioners have contended that the deceased was employed as a Software Engineer in Redisys India Limited and was earning a monthly salary of Rs. 25,000.

The petitioners were financially and emotionally dependent on the deceased, and due to his untimely death, they have suffered immense mental shock, agony, and irreparable loss of the sole breadwinner of the family.
26. In order to establish the employment and income of the deceased, the petitioners examined the HR Manager of Radysis India Ltd as PW-3.
He produced the payslips of the deceased, which are marked as Exhibit P10.

On perusal of the said payslips, it is evident that the deceased was drawing a gross salary of Rs. 25,000/- for the months of August 2023 and September 2023, and after deduction of professional tax, his net monthly salary was Rs.24,800/-.
27.
During the cross-examination of PW-3, learned counsel for the Respondent- no 2 suggested that the deceased was not a permanent employee and was only working as an apprentice.

PW-3,
however, clarified that based on the satisfactory performance of the deceased, his services had been continued by the company.
The evidence of PW-3 further substantiates this position, and there is no material on record to disbelieve either the testimony of PW-3 or the documentary evidence produced.

The payslips at Exhibit P10 are consistent, credible, and duly corroborated by PW-3.
28.

Accordingly, this Tribunal accepts the monthly income of the deceased as Rs. 25,000/-, and after statutory deduction of professional tax, the net monthly income considered for computation is Rs.24,800/-.
29. As the deceased was aged about 23 years, future prospects of 40% is added on the income of the deceased as per Pranay Sethi case.
Then the income would be .34,720/-.
Since, deceased was bachelor, 50% of his income shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Then the income is .17,360/- The loss of dependency would be .17,360 x 12 x 18 =.37,49,760/-.

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold 1 that the Petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled .44,000/- each under the head of filial consortium as the Petitioner No.1 and 2 have lost their son, who was support for them in their old age.

sentences.text: 31. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 have lost their son, who was support for them.
Hence, .20,000/- towards loss to estate.
32. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies Expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances, it would be proper to award .16,500/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral & other incidental expenses.

33. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
 Nature of Compensation Amount  1. Loss of dependency . 37,49,760/-
 2. Loss of Consortium . 88,000/-
 3. Loss to estate . 20,000/-
 4. Transportation of dead body, . 16,500/-
 Funeral & obsequies  Expenses  Total . 38,74,260/-
34.
Liability:
The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of rider of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the RC owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, 50% each is apportioned to petitioner No.1 and 2.

Out of the said apportioned amount 25% each of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner No.1 and 2 in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank for a period of 2 years and balance 75% each shall be disbursed to them through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
